subject: AWS PO: term lifecycle & approvals for HelioHealth
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Apr 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS PO: term lifecycle & approvals for HelioHealth

Hi Maria —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Per our conversation, I wanted to document the private offer options we can present in AWS Marketplace and outline a recommended approval path so procurement and finance have the right artifacts. Key points below:

- Offer options we can create as a Private Offer: 12-month (standard), 18-month (discounted), or 12-month + optional 6-month top-up amendment.
- Pricing: see attached pricing_matrix.xlsx — the 18-month option nets a ~12% discount vs list; the staged 12 + 6 top-up holds the 12-month price for the initial period and allows scaling without a new PO (helps CFO bandwidth).
- Activation & billing notes: AWS Marketplace private offers can be prorated for mid-month activations; however, buyer-side approvals (procurement + CFO) must be completed before seller activates the subscription in the marketplace.
- Evidence pack: we can attach SOC2 summary, network diagram, and data-handling sheet; I attached the current SOW (HelioHealth_SOW_v2.pdf) for legal review.

Ask: can you confirm (a) whether HelioHealth procurement is comfortable with a 12-month PO with optional 6-month amendment, (b) whether your CFO will require an annual-only commitment, and (c) the names/emails for the final signers so we can map approval lanes?

If it helps, Karthik (cc’d) can run a short pricing/demo call with IT/security next week to reassure the team about integration and SSO.

Next steps from our side once you confirm: we’ll prepare the AWS private offer draft, assemble the evidence pack, and circulate a DocuSign PO for signature.

Thanks —
Evelyn Hart
Director, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@heliohealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@heliohealth.com>, Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@heliohealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Apr 2028 09:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: AWS PO: term lifecycle & approvals for HelioHealth

Hi Evelyn —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few quick answers from procurement:

1) Procurement preference is a 12-month PO with the option to extend — our CFO typically resists anything longer than 12 months without a pilot.
2) Evidence pack: please include SOC2 Type II summary and a network diagram. We will want the SOW to show data residency controls.
3) Signers: Procurement will route to Jorge (CFO) for final approval; I’m including Jorge on this thread.

Question: for the staged 12 + 6 amendment, will the optional top-up require a new approval on our side or can it be auto-executed if certain usage thresholds are met? We want to avoid forcing Jorge to re-sign for operational scaling.

Thanks —
Maria
Maria Gomez
Head of Procurement | HelioHealth
maria.gomez@heliohealth.com | +1 212-555-0103
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Apr 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS PO: term lifecycle & approvals for HelioHealth

Evelyn / team —

Good catch from Maria. A few operational clarifications and a recommended approach from our side:

- Amendment behavior: AWS Marketplace private offers don’t support fully automated signature-free extensions tied to usage thresholds. The standard approach we use is a 12-month PO with an amendment clause: at the 9–10 month mark we trigger an internal approval request (seller-side) and prepare a short amendment (DocuSign) that Jorge can sign to add the 6-month top-up without re-negotiating price. That keeps CFO involvement light (single-line approval).

- Risk/reassurance: to reduce CFO friction, we recommend the initial 12-month PO include a 30-day pilot exit clause for the first 90 days and explicit language that the 6-month top-up is an option (not automatic) with pre-agreed price. That usually satisfies finance.

- Pricing detail: attached pricing_matrix.xlsx — shows per-token and per-embedding unit rates, with the discount tiers and the reconciliation method for overage/commit. If HelioHealth expects bursty usage, a staged approach (initial commit + capacity burst buffer) reduces immediate spend risk.

- Approver mapping: Maria -> Procurement (routing), IT security owner (we’ll need a technical contact for the evidence pack), Jorge Alvarez (CFO) final sign-off. If Jorge wants finance to pre-approve an automated top-up threshold we can propose a pre-signed amendment with a defined cap; legal needs to review but it’s often acceptable.

Action items I can take: prepare the amendment language template, finalize the pricing matrix into the private offer payload, and coordinate legal for the DocuSign envelope. Need: the IT security contact email and confirmation from Jorge if he wants the amendment pre-signed or manual.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Apr 2028 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS PO: term lifecycle & approvals for HelioHealth

Hi Maria / Jorge —

Thanks for the quick replies and for looping Jorge in. Per Karthik’s note, here’s the path I propose so we can keep procurement effort minimal and still provide HelioHealth the price certainty you want:

1) We’ll issue a 12-month AWS Marketplace private offer (DocuSign link below) with:
   - an option to add a 6-month top-up via a one-page amendment (pre-drafted but not auto-executed)
   - a 90-day pilot exit window for the initial period
   - explicit data residency and SAML/SSO acceptance shown in the SOW (attached).

2) Evidence pack: I attached the SOW and we will add SOC2 summary + network diagram in the next update.

3) Signing flow: Procurement (Maria) routes -> Jorge (CFO final approval). The amendment will be prepared and held in the DocuSign envelope; if Jorge prefers to pre-approve an amendment up to a fixed cap, we can add that clause — please confirm preferred approach.

DocuSign (draft PO): https://www.docusign.com/1234/HelioHealth_PO
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/3581

If this sounds good I’ll send the DocuSign to Maria for routing. Karthik — please go ahead and finalize the amendment language; Neha, loop legal for a quick review of the SOW/data residency wording. Vanessa, I’ll need you to set the activation window and coordinate marketplace activation once signed.

Thanks —
Evelyn
